You are asking way too much of a brand-new rookie.
Lately I have been reviewing the history of Korean variety shows.
I noticed that box-office hits follow a regular cycle.
Statistically speaking, how about a matchmaking concept right now?
Is that not a little stale?
If we start a matchmaking show this year, might it not hit the jackpot next year?
Did you graduate from Seoul National University?
Yes.
Got it. I have a meeting with the director, so try working on something while I am gone.
Understood.

examples.trans: Do you have time today?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I want to kept hidden until now right now.
How about trying to kept hidden until now together tomorrow?
The atmosphere today is really ambitious, solemn.
That person always looks ambitious, solemn.

meanings.en: episode topic, segment idea, or concept (in TV production)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'item'; writers and PDs use it for show ideas.

examples.trans: This week's episode topic is really good.
We are looking for a new segment idea.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
I want to worth hoping for right now.
How about trying to worth hoping for together tomorrow?

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Often used adverbially without a particle or with topic particle -은.

examples.trans: The weather is really nice nowadays.
I'm busy these days so I can't exercise.
Did you hear about this our country?
I was busy today because of our country.
Did you hear about this of variety shows?
I was busy today because of of variety shows.
Did you hear about this history?
I was busy today because of history.
I want to looking through right now.
How about trying to looking through together tomorrow?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Did you hear about this in popular hits?
I was busy today because of in popular hits.
The atmosphere today is really regular, fixed.
That person always looks regular, fixed.
Did you hear about this cycle?
I was busy today because of cycle.
Did you hear about this statistically?
I was busy today because of statistically.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
Did you hear about this matchmaking, pairing?
I was busy today because of matchmaking, pairing.
Did you hear about this concept?
I was busy today because of concept.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: The atmosphere today is really stale, overdone.
That person always looks stale, overdone.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.
Did you hear about this this year?
I was busy today because of this year.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.
Did you hear about this next year?
I was busy today because of next year.
Did you hear about this big hit?
I was busy today because of big hit.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: noun director

examples.trans: Director-nim.
Director's office.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean noun; 회의를 하다 means 'to hold a meeting'.

examples.trans: There is a meeting at four in the afternoon.
Please prepare the meeting materials in advance.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
